title: Input devices
competency: Identify input devices and explain their functions.

keywords.def: The physical parts of a computer that we can see and touch.
Hardware used to enter data into a computer, e.g. keyboard, mouse, scanner.
An input device with keys for entering text and numbers.
A hand-operated input device that controls the pointer on the screen.
An input device that turns printed text, handwriting or pictures into a digital document.
Optical character recognition: reads printed or handwritten characters and turns them into computer text.
Optical mark recognition: senses pencil marks, e.g. on exam answer sheets.
A device that reads the black-and-white bar codes printed on products.

en.text: Hardware is the physical part of a computer that we can see and touch. Input devices enter data and turn it into 0s and 1s. The keyboard has groups of keys: Esc cancels, Backspace deletes the character before the cursor, function keys (F1–F12) do special tasks, navigation keys move around, Ctrl and Alt combine with other keys, and the numeric keypad enters numbers fast. The mouse controls the pointer: left click selects, right click shows properties, the wheel scrolls.

screens.title: Keyboard key groups
paras: Esc: cancel or close an operation.
Backspace: delete the character before the cursor.
Function keys F1–F12 on the top row: special tasks; F1 is usually Help.
Navigation and editing keys: arrows, Home, End, Page Up, Page Down, Delete, Insert.
Typing (alphanumeric) keys: letters, numbers, punctuation.
Ctrl: with other keys for bold, save, copy, cut, paste.
Windows key: opens the Start Menu; Windows + D shows the desktop, Windows + L locks the computer.
Alt: alternate operations with other keys.
Numeric keypad: enter numbers quickly, like a calculator.

screens.title: The mouse
paras: A mouse controls the movement of the pointer. It is named for its shape.
Left button: select (left click).
Right button: see properties (right click).
Middle button / wheel: scroll.
Mice connect by cable or wirelessly (cordless).

en.text: Other input devices: a scanner turns paper text or pictures into a digital document. Optical recognition systems use light: OCR reads characters, OMR senses pencil marks (used to mark national exams), and a barcode reader reads product codes. A microphone lets speech recognition enter data by voice. A light pen draws on the screen, a touch screen uses your finger (as in ATMs and phones), and a joystick controls games.

screens.title: Marking exams
screens.ask: National exam answer sheets with pencil-filled bubbles are marked by a machine. Which device?
screens.after: Optical Mark Recognition senses pencil marks and compares them with the answer key.

screens.title: More input devices
paras: Scanner: accepts printed text, handwriting or an object and converts it to a digital document.
OCR: reads typed, printed or handwritten characters and compares their shapes with fonts in memory.
OMR: senses the presence or absence of a mark such as pencil marks; used for exams like the ESLCE.
Barcode reader: reads codes (e.g. UPC) on products; used in shops, libraries and stock control.
Speech recognition: a microphone enters speech; the computer acts on it.
Light pen: touches the screen to create or change graphics.
Touch screen: enter data with a finger; used in ATMs, phones, tablets.
Joystick: controls speed and direction in games.
